compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The `rebar-root-disk-pressure` CloudWatch alarm (root `/`, 30G, threshold 85%) sat in ALARM for ~39 hours on 2026-08-04/06: the review-bot host's root disk filled from ~48% to ~95% during an autodeploy build burst, then stayed pinned at 92-96% until the next real deploy finally reclaimed it. Root cause: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` reclaims docker garbage via `prune_docker_caches()` (builder prune `--keep-storage 5GB` + image prune) ONLY on the deploy and backoff paths. When `main` is quiescent, every ~2-min `rebar-autodeploy.timer` tick hits the "up to date … no-op" early exit (autodeploy.sh:228) and returns WITHOUT pruning, so nothing reclaims disk between deploys. This extends closed bug 7a41-95f4-c38c-4b5a (added the deploy-path prune) to cover the quiescent-main gap it left.

## Approach

Add a pressure-triggered, throttled reclaim to the autodeploy no-op path — the ideal hook because it fires every ~2 min exactly when no deploy is reclaiming, already holds the single-flight `flock` (autodeploy.sh:191), and already has `prune_docker_caches()` in scope. Reuse the exact root-disk-% computation from observability.sh:79 (`df --output=pcent /`).

1. Add tunables near `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP` (autodeploy.sh:~87): `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` (default 80 — below the 85% alarm for hysteresis), `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL` (default 600s throttle), `PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE` (default under `STATE_DIR`).
2. **Relocate `prune_docker_caches()` above the no-op exit.** It is currently defined at autodeploy.sh:245, which is AFTER the line-228 no-op exit; bash only makes a function callable once its `funcname() { … }` definition line has executed, so calling it from line 228 would fail with "command not found". Move the entire `prune_docker_caches()` definition up into the helper block near line ~150 (immediately below the new helpers in step 3), so it is defined before its FIRST use. Its existing callers stay valid because they all run later than line 150: `record_backoff_failure` (autodeploy.sh:261), the deploy-success path (autodeploy.sh:379), and the new line-228 call. Concrete resulting order: helpers/`prune_docker_caches`/`reclaim_under_pressure` at ~142-160 → single-flight + fetch (~191-224) → line-228 no-op exit calling `reclaim_under_pressure` → backoff/deploy paths (245+) that also call `prune_docker_caches`. `prune_docker_caches`' own body is unchanged (it uses only `docker`, `timeout`, `log`, `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP`, all available at that point).

3. Add two helpers in that same block (autodeploy.sh:~150): `root_disk_pct()` (the `df --output=pcent /` one-liner) and `reclaim_under_pressure()` which returns early unless `root_disk_pct >= DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`, enforces the min-interval throttle via the persisted timestamp file (atomic tmp+mv write), emits a countable `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` journal marker via the existing `marker()`, calls `prune_docker_caches` (now defined above it), and logs the before/after percentage. A prune failure only logs (never alters control flow), matching the deploy-path guarantees.
4. Call `reclaim_under_pressure` on the no-op early-exit line (autodeploy.sh:228), before the `log "up to date"; exit 0`.

Default threshold 80% with a flat floor plus the 10-min throttle (not a derivative/trend) is chosen deliberately: the throttle prevents per-tick churn and `prune_docker_caches` keeps a 5GB warm cache so back-to-back prunes are cheap no-ops; an absolute floor is simpler and less flappy than slope tracking. All new behavior is opt-outable via env overrides sourced from `/etc/rebar/autodeploy.env` (already sourced by the script), so no host redeploy is required to tune it.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — add the three tunables; relocate the existing `prune_docker_caches()` definition from line ~245 up into the helper block (~150) so it precedes the new line-228 call site (its body and its two existing call sites are otherwise unchanged); add the `root_disk_pct()` + `reclaim_under_pressure()` helpers; and add the single new call site on the no-op exit path (line 228). No change to the deploy/backoff prune BEHAVIOR, the drain/defer logic, or any journal-marker token except the new `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE`.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py` — new test module (new testable behavior): assert the reclaim fires when simulated disk% is at/above the threshold and no-ops below it, that the throttle suppresses a second prune inside the interval, and that a prune failure does not change the script's exit code. Stub `df` and `docker` via PATH shims / injected fakes, matching the existing `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_*` harness style.

The new `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` marker is intentionally NOT wired to a new CloudWatch metric in this story (autodeploy still exits 0; the existing `root_disk_used_percent` alarm already covers the outcome). Wiring an observability delta metric for it is deferred as out of scope.

## Testing

- Happy path: with a `df` shim reporting 90% and a `docker` shim that records calls, running the no-op path invokes `prune_docker_caches` once and writes the timestamp file.
- Throttle/edge path: a second invocation within `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL` does NOT invoke prune; an invocation with `df` reporting 70% (below threshold) does NOT invoke prune.
- Failure path: a `docker` shim that exits non-zero leaves the script's overall exit status at 0 (prune failure is non-fatal), and the pressure marker is still emitted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On the autodeploy no-op tick, when root `/` usage is >= `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` (default 80) and the throttle window has elapsed, `prune_docker_caches` runs — verified by `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py` happy-path assertion (docker-shim call recorded).
- [ ] When root usage is below the threshold, or within the throttle window of the last pressure-prune, no prune runs — verified by the below-threshold and throttle assertions in the same test module.
- [ ] A prune failure on the pressure path does not change autodeploy's exit code (stays 0) and only logs — verified by the failure-path assertion.
- [ ] A countable `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` marker line (prefix `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE ` followed by the `marker()` JSON) is emitted to stderr exactly once per triggered pressure prune and zero times on the below-threshold and throttled paths — asserted by capturing the script's stderr in the test module and counting matches.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the new and existing `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_*` tests pass under the repo venv.

file_impact.reason: add DISK_PRESSURE_PCT/PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL/PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE tunables, root_disk_pct() + reclaim_under_pressure() helpers, and call reclaim_under_pressure on the no-op early-exit path (line ~228)
new test module: pressure prune fires at/above threshold, no-ops below threshold and within the throttle window, and a prune failure keeps exit code 0 with the AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE marker emitted
